page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features 12 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the average tier for general CPU and memory tasks, but it demonstrates strong capabilities in specific workloads. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 21080.54, and the PassMark CPU score is 20085.48. Large block memory read bandwidth reaches 102.38 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 53.61 GB/sec. In LLM inference testing, the server achieves top-tier performance for prompt processing, reaching 8665.1 tokens/sec with a small 135M model and 613.27 tokens/sec with a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are moderate, yielding 32.35 tokens/sec on the 7B model.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential performance consistency tradeoff under sustained, high-intensity CPU workloads. However, the high system memory density of 10.67 GB per core combined with dual NVIDIA Ampere GPUs makes this server a cost-efficient option for GPU-accelerated tasks that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It is well-suited for workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, video streaming transcoding, and database operations requiring moderate local NVMe storage.
